species.name: Gerbil
mustRead: furred tail as long as the body with a dark tuft at the tip
elongated hind feet
large dark eyes on a pointed face

species.name: Wild Sheep
mustRead: massive spiralling horns curling beside the head
short coarse hair coat, not woolly fleece
muscular blocky body on sturdy legs
species.note: Read as a representative argali/bighorn type. Wild sheep are hair-coated and athletic, not fluffy like a domestic sheep.

species.name: Hyrax
mustRead: tailless rounded guinea-pig-like body
short blunt muzzle with long whiskers
small rounded ears and stubby legs

species.name: Bactrian Camel
mustRead: two separate humps
shaggy hanging hair on the neck, chest and hump crowns
long curved neck and long legs

species.name: Wildcat
mustRead: thick blunt-ended tail with dark rings and a black tip
broad head with a striped tabby coat
sturdy build heavier than a house cat

species.name: Polar Bear
mustRead: long neck with a small narrow Roman-nosed head
huge furred paws
sloping shoulders on a long body
species.note: Head is smaller and the neck far longer than on a brown bear, and there is no shoulder hump.

species.name: Musk Ox
mustRead: curtain of hair hanging almost to the hooves
horns meeting in a helmet-like boss across the forehead then hooking down and out
humped shoulders with the head carried low

species.name: Walrus
mustRead: pair of long downward tusks
dense bristle moustache on a squared muzzle
vast wrinkled blubbery body on short flippers

species.name: Seal
mustRead: smooth torpedo body with no external ear flaps
hind flippers trailing straight back, unable to fold under the body
round dog-like head with large dark eyes and whiskers
species.note: Generic name read as a representative true seal (harbour seal). It humps along on its belly; drawing it propped up on rotated hind flippers makes it a sea lion.

species.name: Fur Seal
mustRead: small external ear flaps
very long fore-flippers propping the chest up
dog-like whiskered muzzle
species.note: Unlike a true seal it walks on all fours with hind flippers rotated forward.

species.name: Bear
mustRead: muscular shoulder hump over the forelegs
small rounded ears on a broad dished head
flat-footed plantigrade paws and a stub tail

species.name: Olm
mustRead: pale pink translucent eel-like body
bushy red external gills behind the head
tiny spindly legs with three toes
species.note: Eyes are skinned over and invisible; the limbs are vestigially thin, not lizard-like.

species.name: Wild Pig
mustRead: long wedge snout ending in a flat disc nose
high shoulder hump with a bristly crest mane
short upward-curving tusks

species.name: Gharial
mustRead: extremely long needle-thin snout studded with interlocking teeth
bulbous pot knob on the snout tip of males
tall laterally flattened paddle tail

species.name: Giant Otter
mustRead: broad flattened paddle-like tail
cream throat bib patch
flat whiskered head with short round ears
species.note: Its tail is wide and flattened like a rudder, not round and tapering like a river otter's.

species.name: Water Vole
mustRead: blunt rounded muzzle with a chubby face
small ears almost buried in fur
short furred tail about half the body length
species.note: Not a rat - blunt face, tiny hidden ears, and a furry rather than scaly tail.

species.name: Sea Turtle
mustRead: flattened teardrop shell
long wing-like front flippers
blunt beaked head that cannot retract
species.note: Unlike a land tortoise the shell is low and streamlined and the head and limbs never withdraw.

species.name: Sea Lion
mustRead: small external ear flaps
long fore-flippers lifting the chest clear of the ground
blunt dog-like whiskered muzzle
species.note: Walks on all fours with hind flippers rotated forward - a true seal cannot, and has no ear flaps.

species.name: Coastal Lizard
mustRead: long tapering tail longer than the body
sprawling bent-elbow limbs with splayed clawed toes
scaly wedge head with a visible ear opening
species.note: Generic name - interpreted as a rock/side-blotched lizard type.

species.name: Sea Otter
mustRead: floats belly-up on its back, often with a rock on the chest
blunt round face packed with pale whiskers
webbed flipper-like hind feet
species.note: Much bulkier and blunter-faced than a river otter, and habitually drawn on its back rather than running.

species.name: Marsh Rodent
mustRead: blunt rounded head with large orange incisors
long scaly rope-like tail
partly webbed hind feet
species.note: Generic name - interpreted as a muskrat/coypu type semi-aquatic rodent.

species.name: Rat
mustRead: long naked scaly tail about as long as the body
pointed twitching snout with long whiskers
rounded ears and hunched arched back
species.note: aspect includes the tail; body alone is about 2.6 wide to tall

species.name: Cat
mustRead: triangular upright ears on a round short-muzzled head
long expressive tail
vertical slit pupils and long whiskers

species.name: Iguana
mustRead: row of spiny crest scales from the nape down the back
loose dewlap flap under the chin
banded tail far longer than the body
species.note: aspect includes the tail, which is roughly two-thirds of the total length
